recommendations.statement: Don't do imaging for low back pain within the first six weeks unless red flags are present.
recommendations.precondition: acute low back pain of less than 6 weeks with no red flags (major trauma, neurological deficit, history of cancer, unexplained weight loss, fever/infection, IV drug use)
recommendations.consider_instead: conservative management with reassessment; image only if red flags emerge or symptoms persist beyond 6 weeks
recommendations.rationale: Imaging of the low back before six weeks does not improve outcomes but exposes patients to unnecessary cost, radiation, and incidental findings that prompt further low-value testing.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't routinely prescribe antibiotics for uncomplicated upper respiratory infections or mild acute rhinosinusitis.
recommendations.precondition: uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection, or acute rhinosinusitis with mild-to-moderate symptoms of less than 7 days
recommendations.consider_instead: symptomatic treatment; reserve antibiotics for persistent (>10 days), severe, or worsening ('double-sickening') presentations
recommendations.rationale: Most acute URIs and sinusitis are viral and self-limited; antibiotics do not speed recovery and drive resistance and adverse effects.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't obtain routine preoperative chest radiographs, ECGs, or laboratory tests in asymptomatic patients undergoing low-risk surgery.
recommendations.precondition: asymptomatic patient with no active cardiopulmonary disease undergoing low-risk / minor surgery
recommendations.consider_instead: test selectively based on history, examination, and the specific procedure
recommendations.rationale: Routine preoperative testing in asymptomatic patients for low-risk surgery rarely changes management and generates false positives and downstream testing.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't screen for prostate cancer using a PSA test without a discussion of the risks and benefits.
recommendations.precondition: asymptomatic average-risk man, particularly under 55 or over 69 years, without shared decision-making
recommendations.consider_instead: shared decision-making before any PSA testing
recommendations.rationale: PSA screening without informed discussion leads to over-diagnosis and over-treatment of indolent disease with significant harms.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't perform neuroimaging (CT or MRI) for patients with stable headaches that meet criteria for migraine.
recommendations.precondition: recurrent headaches meeting migraine criteria, stable pattern, normal neurological examination, no red flags
recommendations.consider_instead: clinical diagnosis; image only for red flags (thunderclap onset, new/progressive deficit, immunosuppression, age >50 new headache)
recommendations.rationale: Neuroimaging in stable migraine without red flags almost never reveals significant pathology and drives incidentalomas and cost.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't use benzodiazepines or other sedative-hypnotics in older adults as the first choice for insomnia, agitation, or delirium.
recommendations.precondition: older adult (typically 65+) with insomnia, agitation, or delirium
recommendations.consider_instead: non-pharmacological measures first; treat underlying causes
recommendations.rationale: Older adults are more sensitive to benzodiazepines, with markedly increased risk of cognitive impairment, falls, fractures, and motor-vehicle crashes.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't transfuse red blood cells for arbitrary hemoglobin or hematocrit thresholds in the absence of symptoms, active bleeding, or hemodynamic instability.
recommendations.precondition: hemodynamically stable, non-bleeding hospitalized patient with hemoglobin at or above the restrictive threshold (7-8 g/dL)
recommendations.consider_instead: restrictive transfusion strategy; transfuse for symptoms rather than a number
recommendations.rationale: A restrictive transfusion threshold is as safe as or safer than liberal transfusion and avoids the costs and risks of unnecessary blood products.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't repeat colorectal cancer screening by colonoscopy for 10 years after a high-quality normal colonoscopy in average-risk individuals.
recommendations.precondition: average-risk individual with a prior high-quality colonoscopy that was normal, within the last 10 years
recommendations.consider_instead: resume screening at the guideline-recommended 10-year interval
recommendations.rationale: Repeating colonoscopy sooner than 10 years after a normal high-quality examination in average-risk patients adds risk and cost without benefit.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't perform stress cardiac imaging or coronary angiography in patients without cardiac symptoms unless high-risk markers are present.
recommendations.precondition: asymptomatic patient at low risk for coronary artery disease, without high-risk markers, being considered for screening stress cardiac imaging or coronary angiography; does NOT apply to coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring obtained to refine risk and guide statin decision-making in an intermediate-risk adult (2018 ACC/AHA cholesterol guideline)
recommendations.consider_instead: risk-factor assessment and modification; test only symptomatic or high-risk patients
recommendations.rationale: Screening stress imaging in asymptomatic low-risk patients rarely changes management and leads to false positives, radiation, and invasive follow-up.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised. Precondition narrowed 15-Jul-2026 (Batch-1 catalog-expansion kickoff, ratified by V): CAC scoring for intermediate-risk statin decision-making is explicitly out of scope; stress imaging / angiography screening in asymptomatic low-risk patients remains in scope.

recommendations.statement: Don't use advanced imaging (PET, CT, or radionuclide bone scans) to stage early breast or prostate cancer at low risk for metastasis.
recommendations.precondition: newly diagnosed early-stage, low-risk breast or prostate cancer without signs or symptoms of metastasis
recommendations.consider_instead: reserve advanced staging imaging for higher-stage or symptomatic disease
recommendations.rationale: Advanced imaging to stage low-risk early cancers has a very low yield of true metastases and generates false positives, cost, and radiation.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't use antimicrobials to treat asymptomatic bacteriuria.
recommendations.precondition: positive urine culture in a patient with no urinary symptoms (excluding pregnancy and pre-urologic-procedure settings)
recommendations.consider_instead: no treatment; treat only symptomatic urinary tract infection
recommendations.rationale: Treating asymptomatic bacteriuria does not improve outcomes and promotes resistance, C. difficile, and drug adverse effects.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't prescribe stress ulcer prophylaxis to medical inpatients unless they are at high risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
recommendations.precondition: medical inpatient outside the ICU without high-risk features for GI bleeding (mechanical ventilation, coagulopathy, GI bleed history)
recommendations.consider_instead: reserve acid suppression for patients meeting high-risk criteria
recommendations.rationale: Routine stress ulcer prophylaxis in low-risk inpatients does not prevent clinically important bleeding and increases pneumonia and C. difficile risk.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't obtain CT scans in children with minor head injuries who are low-risk by validated clinical criteria.
recommendations.precondition: child with minor head injury classified as low-risk by a validated decision rule (e.g. PECARN)
recommendations.consider_instead: observation and validated decision rules rather than routine CT
recommendations.rationale: CT in low-risk minor pediatric head injury rarely finds significant injury and exposes children to ionizing radiation and future cancer risk.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Avoid CT of the head in adults with minor head injury who are at low risk based on validated decision rules.
recommendations.precondition: adult with minor head injury who is low-risk by a validated decision rule (e.g. Canadian CT Head Rule)
recommendations.consider_instead: apply validated decision rules; observe rather than scan low-risk patients
recommendations.rationale: Validated decision rules safely identify adults with minor head injury who do not need CT, reducing radiation and cost.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't routinely order a thyroid ultrasound in patients with abnormal thyroid function tests if there is no palpable abnormality of the thyroid gland.
recommendations.precondition: abnormal TSH or thyroid function tests without a palpable thyroid nodule or goiter
recommendations.consider_instead: ultrasound only when a nodule is palpable or incidentally found
recommendations.rationale: Thyroid ultrasound for abnormal function tests without a palpable nodule detects clinically insignificant nodules and drives unnecessary biopsies.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't obtain screening resting or exercise electrocardiograms in asymptomatic adults at low risk for coronary heart disease.
recommendations.precondition: asymptomatic adult at low risk for coronary heart disease undergoing routine health assessment
recommendations.consider_instead: cardiovascular risk-factor assessment instead of screening ECG
recommendations.rationale: Screening ECGs in low-risk asymptomatic adults rarely change management and lead to false positives and a cascade of further testing.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't perform DEXA (bone density) screening for osteoporosis in women younger than 65 or men younger than 70 with no risk factors.
recommendations.precondition: woman under 65 or man under 70 with no osteoporosis risk factors
recommendations.consider_instead: screen at the guideline age, or earlier only if risk factors are present
recommendations.rationale: Bone-density screening in younger low-risk adults has low yield and can lead to unnecessary treatment.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't perform repetitive daily laboratory testing (such as CBC and chemistry panels) in the face of clinical and laboratory stability.
recommendations.precondition: clinically stable hospitalized patient with stable laboratory values
recommendations.consider_instead: order labs to answer a specific clinical question rather than by daily routine
recommendations.rationale: Repetitive daily labs in stable inpatients contribute to iatrogenic anemia, false positives, patient discomfort, and cost without changing management.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the well-established ABIM Choosing Wisely clinician lists; substance is stable/canonical. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Do not delay or avoid palliative care for a patient with metastatic cancer because they are pursuing disease-directed treatment.
recommendations.precondition: patient with metastatic cancer who is receiving or pursuing disease-directed treatment (chemotherapy or radiotherapy)
recommendations.consider_instead: integrate early palliative care alongside disease-directed treatment
recommendations.rationale: Randomised trials show early palliative care improves pain and symptom control, family satisfaction, and quality of life, reduces cost, and increases survival in selected populations; it can enhance the benefits of cancer-directed treatment.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Avoid chemotherapy and instead focus on symptom relief and palliative care for patients with advanced cancer unlikely to benefit from chemotherapy.
recommendations.precondition: advanced solid-organ cancer with one or more of: performance status 3 or 4, no benefit from previous evidence-based interventions, not suitable for a clinical trial, and no evidence supporting further anticancer treatment
recommendations.consider_instead: symptom relief and palliative care
recommendations.rationale: Cancer-directed therapies are unlikely to be effective for markedly debilitated patients (performance status 3-4); appropriate symptom control and palliative care substantially improve quality of life.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not order tests to detect recurrent cancer in asymptomatic patients if there is not a realistic expectation that early detection of recurrence can improve survival or quality of life.
recommendations.precondition: asymptomatic patient on follow-up where early detection of recurrence is not expected to improve survival or quality of life (most solid tumours)
recommendations.consider_instead: symptom-directed follow-up; reserve surveillance testing for cancers where early recurrence detection changes outcomes
recommendations.rationale: For most solid tumours there is no evidence that earlier detection of recurrence improves outcomes; the value of biomarkers, PET/CT and CT scans, endoscopy, and radionuclide scans must be balanced against the harm and anxiety of extensive follow-up testing.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not order PET/CT scans to monitor response to palliative chemotherapy.
recommendations.precondition: patient on palliative-intent chemotherapy for advanced cancer, being monitored for treatment response
recommendations.consider_instead: clinical assessment and conventional imaging as indicated; use PET/CT only within a clinical trial
recommendations.rationale: Existing evidence does not support PET/CT to monitor response to palliative chemotherapy; no reliable evidence shows it improves survival or quality of life, so it should not be used outside a clinical trial.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not decide treatment for potentially curable cancers without inputs from a multidisciplinary oncology team.
recommendations.precondition: potentially curable cancer requiring multimodality therapy (e.g. oral cavity, cervix, lung)
recommendations.consider_instead: present the case to a multidisciplinary tumour board or clinic before deciding treatment
recommendations.rationale: Multidisciplinary team care improves staging accuracy, processes of care, and guideline concordance; the stakes are especially high for potentially curable disease.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not treat patients with advanced metastatic cancer in the intensive care unit unless there is an acutely reversible event.
recommendations.precondition: advanced metastatic cancer with life expectancy under 1 year and no acutely reversible cause for deterioration
recommendations.consider_instead: goals-of-care discussion and palliative management outside the ICU
recommendations.rationale: Prognosis is poor and ICU care is likely futile unless the cause of admission is reversible; international groups recommend against ICU admission for advanced metastatic cancer with life expectancy under 1 year.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not use advanced radiation techniques where conventional radiation can be just as effective.
recommendations.precondition: radiotherapy where conventional technique is equally effective and no level-1 evidence supports the advanced technique's superiority for that site
recommendations.consider_instead: conventional radiotherapy; reserve advanced techniques for scenarios with clear evidence of superiority
recommendations.rationale: Conventional radiotherapy costs a fraction of advanced therapy (especially out-of-pocket); no level-1 evidence shows advanced techniques improve overall survival in general, though they help selected sites.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not deliver care in a high-cost setting when it could be delivered just as effectively in a lower-cost setting.
recommendations.precondition: routine or low-risk cancer care and follow-up that could be delivered closer to home at a lower-cost local or regional facility
recommendations.consider_instead: a hub-and-spoke model: routine/low-risk care closer to home, complex cases referred to tertiary centres
recommendations.rationale: Surveillance and routine care after definitive treatment can be delivered equally well locally and is more patient-centred; patients often travel vast distances for care that could be delivered closer to home.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not initiate whole breast radiotherapy in 25 fractions as part of breast conservation therapy in women aged 50 years and older with early-stage invasive breast cancer without considering shorter treatment schedules.
recommendations.precondition: woman aged 50 years or older with early-stage invasive breast cancer undergoing whole-breast radiotherapy after breast conservation surgery
recommendations.consider_instead: consider hypofractionated schedules (approximately 3-4 weeks), which show equivalent tumour control and cosmesis
recommendations.rationale: Evidence shows equivalent tumour control and cosmetic outcome with shorter (~3-4 week) hypofractionated schedules in specific populations; patients and physicians should consider these before a 25-fraction course.
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Do not use white-cell stimulating factors for primary prevention of febrile neutropenia for patients with less than 20% risk for this complication.
recommendations.precondition: chemotherapy regimen with less than approximately 20% risk of febrile neutropenia, with effective alternative regimens available and no patient-specific high-risk features (age, medical history, disease characteristics)
recommendations.consider_instead: reserve G-CSF primary prophylaxis for regimens with ~20% or greater febrile-neutropenia risk, or for high-risk patients
recommendations.rationale: International guidelines recommend white-cell stimulating factors when febrile-neutropenia risk is approximately 20% and no effective alternative regimen exists; below that threshold, routine primary prophylaxis is low-value unless patient-specific high-risk features are present.
keywords: white cell stimulating factor febrile neutropenia
recommendations.notes: NCG India Choosing Wisely — statement VERBATIM from Pramesh CS et al, Lancet Oncol 2019;20(4):e218-e223 (Table); rationale abridged from the paper. Source PDF supplied by V.

recommendations.statement: Don't perform imaging of the carotid arteries for simple syncope without other neurologic symptoms.
recommendations.precondition: simple syncope (faint) with no focal neurologic symptoms or signs
recommendations.consider_instead: history, examination, orthostatic vitals and a 12-lead ECG; reserve carotid imaging for suspected cerebrovascular disease with focal signs
recommendations.rationale: Occlusive carotid disease does not cause syncope; carotid imaging in simple syncope has no diagnostic yield, adds cost, and can trigger downstream cascades.
recommendations.notes: AI-transcribed from the AAN ABIM Choosing Wisely five-things list (canonical, stable). Inserted per the Right-Care fixes PRD (13-Jul-2026, Fix B — the C04 catalog gap); wording per the kickoff draft, flagged for V ratification. Spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Avoid CT of the head in patients with syncope and a normal neurological exam and no head trauma.
recommendations.precondition: syncope with a normal neurological examination and no head trauma
recommendations.consider_instead: history, examination, orthostatic vitals and a 12-lead ECG; image only for focal neurologic findings or head injury
recommendations.rationale: Routine neuroimaging is not indicated in syncope absent focal neurologic findings or head trauma (2017 ACC/AHA/HRS syncope guideline); yield is negligible and radiation/cost are not.
recommendations.notes: Guideline-derived (2017 ACC/AHA/HRS syncope guideline), not an ABIM Choosing Wisely list item — cwus-class provenance per the Right-Care fixes PRD (13-Jul-2026, Fix B). Wording per the kickoff draft, flagged for V ratification of wording + attribution. The corpus chunk's fixed '(Choosing Wisely, US, 2017)' source suffix slightly mislabels this row — cosmetic, noted in the build report.

recommendations.society: Indian Council of Medical Research (AMR guidelines)
recommendations.statement: Do not prescribe antibiotics or antiprotozoals for acute non-dysenteric diarrhoea or gastroenteritis when there is no fever and no blood in the stool.
recommendations.precondition: acute non-dysenteric diarrhoea or gastroenteritis with no fever and no blood in stool
recommendations.consider_instead: oral rehydration and symptomatic care; reassess if fever, blood in stool, or dehydration develops
recommendations.rationale: Most acute watery diarrhoea is viral and self-limited; empiric antibiotic-antiprotozoal combinations (e.g. fluoroquinolone + nitroimidazole) do not shorten the illness and drive antimicrobial resistance and adverse effects.
recommendations.notes: Guideline-derived (ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes 2019; IDSA/ACG acute-diarrhoea themes), not an ABIM Choosing Wisely list item. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Statement/rationale/keywords AI-drafted; attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised.

recommendations.society: Indian Council of Medical Research (AMR guidelines)
recommendations.statement: Do not start empiric antibiotics for acute undifferentiated fever of less than 5 days without a localising source or red flags.
recommendations.precondition: acute undifferentiated fever of less than 5 days duration with no localising source on history and examination and no red flags (haemodynamic instability, altered sensorium, severe dehydration, immunocompromise)
recommendations.consider_instead: symptomatic treatment, hydration, and planned review; targeted testing (e.g. malaria smear, dengue serology as locally indicated) before any antimicrobial
recommendations.rationale: Acute undifferentiated short-duration fever in the outpatient setting is most often viral or vector-borne, where empiric antibacterials do not help; they add adverse effects and drive resistance (WHO AWaRe stewardship).
recommendations.notes: Guideline-derived (ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes 2019; WHO AWaRe), not an ABIM Choosing Wisely list item. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Statement/rationale/keywords AI-drafted; attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't prescribe antibiotics for acute pharyngitis without confirmed or high-probability group A streptococcal infection.
recommendations.precondition: acute pharyngitis without laboratory confirmation of group A streptococcus and without a high-probability presentation (low Centor/McIsaac score)
recommendations.consider_instead: symptomatic treatment; apply a validated score (Centor/McIsaac) and confirm strep (RADT/culture) before antibiotics
recommendations.rationale: Most acute sore throats are viral; antibiotics without strep confirmation do not shorten illness and expose patients to adverse effects and resistance.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from IDSA pharyngitis guidance / Choosing Wisely AAFP themes. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't prescribe antibiotics for acute bronchitis in otherwise healthy adults without evidence of pneumonia.
recommendations.precondition: acute bronchitis or acute cough illness in an otherwise healthy adult with no clinical or radiographic evidence of pneumonia (no consolidation)
recommendations.consider_instead: symptomatic treatment and safety-netting; reassess for pneumonia if focal chest findings, hypoxia, or deterioration
recommendations.rationale: Acute bronchitis is overwhelmingly viral; antibiotics (including respiratory fluoroquinolones) do not shorten the illness and add adverse effects and resistance.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from Choosing Wisely AAFP/ACCP acute-bronchitis themes. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised. No standalone AAFP CW acute-bronchitis item; nearest CW URI item is IDSA-attributed. Anchored on AFP 2016 clinical review + Cochrane (no net benefit). Reconciliation re-seed 16-Jul-2026: vv:true — verified against a real source (AFP 2016 clinical review + Cochrane, no net benefit); framing paraphrases (no standalone AAFP Choosing Wisely acute-bronchitis item), not a verbatim quote. Kept clinician-facing.

recommendations.statement: Don't use systemic (oral) antibiotics for mild comedonal or mildly inflammatory acne; topical therapy is first-line.
recommendations.precondition: mild acne — comedonal or with few inflammatory papules/pustules — without moderate-to-severe inflammatory or nodulocystic disease
recommendations.consider_instead: topical retinoid with or without benzoyl peroxide / topical antimicrobials as first-line
recommendations.rationale: Systemic antibiotics for mild acne add resistance and adverse effects without benefit over effective topical first-line therapy.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from AAD Choosing Wisely acne themes. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised. Re-anchored to AAD 2024 Guidelines of Care for Acne Vulgaris (antibiotic stewardship); AAD Choosing Wisely list has no acne-antibiotic item. Kept clinician-facing.

recommendations.statement: Don't obtain MRI for chronic or recurrent low back pain without red flags and without documented failed conservative care.
recommendations.precondition: chronic or recurrent low back pain (more than 6 weeks, or relapsing over months to years) with no red flags (radiculopathy or neurological deficit, major trauma, history of cancer, unexplained weight loss, fever/infection, immunosuppression) and no documented trial of failed conservative care
recommendations.consider_instead: structured conservative management (activity, analgesia, physiotherapy) with reassessment; image if red flags emerge or a specific intervention is planned
recommendations.rationale: MRI in chronic low back pain without red flags correlates poorly with symptoms, rarely changes management, and triggers incidental-finding cascades and unnecessary intervention.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from ACP / Choosing Wisely AAFP-ACR low-back-imaging themes; complements cwus-aafp-001, which covers ACUTE (<6wk) low back pain only. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised. ACP High-Value Care imaging advice (2011); addresses non-specific/acute LBP — this rec's 'chronic + failed conservative care' precondition is additive beyond the source (flagged; precondition unchanged).

recommendations.society: Arthroscopy Association of Canada (Choosing Wisely Canada)
recommendations.statement: Don't order MRI of the knee for atraumatic knee pain with a degenerative clinical picture before weight-bearing radiographs.
recommendations.precondition: atraumatic knee pain with a degenerative picture (crepitus, chronicity, age-consistent osteoarthritis features) and no weight-bearing X-ray yet performed; does not apply when examination suggests internal derangement (e.g. positive McMurray or Lachman) or acute trauma
recommendations.consider_instead: weight-bearing (standing) knee radiographs first; MRI only if examination suggests internal derangement or surgery is being planned
recommendations.rationale: In degenerative knee pain, weight-bearing X-rays establish the diagnosis at a fraction of the cost; age-related meniscal MRI signal is near-universal and drives unnecessary arthroscopy.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from AAOS / Choosing Wisely degenerative-knee imaging themes. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised. Re-attributed to Choosing Wisely Canada / Arthroscopy Assoc. of Canada (2024, OA-context); no US AAOS Choosing Wisely knee-imaging item exists. id prefix 'aaos' is legacy — kept as stable key. AAOS AUC is a US alternative anchor if preferred.

recommendations.society: American Society for Clinical Laboratory Science / ASCP (Choosing Wisely)
recommendations.statement: Don't repeat HbA1c testing sooner than the guideline interval when a recent result exists (every 3 years if normal; annually if stable prediabetes).
recommendations.precondition: a recent HbA1c result exists (normal within the last 3 years, or stable prediabetes within the last year) and a repeat is ordered sooner than the guideline interval without a change in clinical status or therapy
recommendations.consider_instead: retrieve and act on the prior result; retest at the guideline interval or when clinical status or therapy changes
recommendations.rationale: HbA1c reflects ~3 months of glycaemia and changes slowly; repeating it inside the guideline interval in stable patients cannot change management and adds cost.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from ADA screening-interval guidance / Choosing Wisely SGIM themes. Re-attributed to ASCLS/ASCP Choosing Wisely (via AAFP mirror; page shows no year). Precondition cites ADA screening intervals but this item is about monitoring cadence (>=3 months) — precondition text left unchanged, flagged for a later clinical refinement. Batch-1 catalog expansion (15-Jul-2026 kickoff); precondition wording ratified by V 15 Jul 2026. Attribution fields inferred — spot-check advised.

recommendations.statement: Don't repeat thyroid function testing in a clinically euthyroid, stable patient sooner than the recommended interval.
recommendations.precondition: clinically euthyroid, stable patient with a recent thyroid function result, re-tested sooner than the recommended interval without new symptoms, pregnancy, or a change in therapy; does not apply to planned recheck of a previously abnormal result
recommendations.consider_instead: use the prior result; retest at guideline intervals (e.g. ~6 weeks after a dose change, then annually once stable) or when symptoms change
recommendations.rationale: TSH moves slowly; early re-testing in stable euthyroid patients yields no actionable change and generates false-positive cascades.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from AACE / Choosing Wisely thyroid-testing themes. PROVISIONAL — no clean single-society source located; verbatim_verified:false. recommendations.statement: Don't repeat lipid panels sooner than the guideline interval in patients at goal or with a recent normal result.
recommendations.precondition: patient at lipid goal or with a recent normal lipid panel, without new cardiovascular events or a change in lipid-lowering therapy, re-tested sooner than the guideline interval
recommendations.consider_instead: use the prior panel; repeat at guideline intervals (typically 4-12 weeks after a therapy change, then annually or less often when stable)
recommendations.rationale: Lipid values are stable over months in unchanged patients; early repeats do not alter therapy and add cost.

recommendations.statement: Don't routinely test vitamin D levels (25-hydroxyvitamin D) in asymptomatic adults without a specific risk factor or indication.
recommendations.precondition: asymptomatic adult with no specific risk factor or indication for vitamin D deficiency (e.g. malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, osteoporosis or fragility fracture, medications affecting vitamin D metabolism)
recommendations.consider_instead: lifestyle advice and empiric supplementation where appropriate; reserve testing for patients with a specific indication
recommendations.rationale: Population vitamin D testing in asymptomatic adults is high-volume and low-yield; results rarely change management compared with empiric advice.
recommendations.notes: AI-drafted from AACE / Endocrine Society / Choosing Wisely vitamin-D screening themes. Note-decidable coverage rec (no gold case bound in Batch-1). recommendations.statement: Don't routinely test vitamin B12 levels in patients without symptoms or risk factors for deficiency.
recommendations.precondition: no symptoms (unexplained anaemia, neuropathy, cognitive change, glossitis) and no risk factors (metformin or long-term PPI use, vegan diet, malabsorption, gastric surgery) for vitamin B12 deficiency
recommendations.consider_instead: test only when symptoms or risk factors for deficiency are present
recommendations.rationale: Routine B12 testing in asymptomatic low-risk patients yields borderline results that trigger cascades without improving outcomes.

recommendations.statement: Don't obtain advanced spinal imaging (MRI or CT) when there are no red flags and no localizing neurological indication.
recommendations.precondition: limb or regional pain being evaluated for a possible spinal cause, with NO focal or progressive neurological deficit, NO neurogenic claudication or radiculopathy, NO saddle anaesthesia or bowel/bladder dysfunction, and NO other red flags (major trauma, cancer history, unexplained weight loss, fever/infection, IV drug use, immunosuppression); a plausible non-spinal cause has already been evaluated (e.g., normal venous Doppler, specialist review advising no intervention). An order for whole-spine or multi-region 'screening' MRI in this setting is low-value.
recommendations.consider_instead: if a spinal cause is genuinely suspected, image only the symptomatic region guided by a localizing exam finding rather than screening the whole spine; otherwise continue conservative management and reassess, escalating only if a red flag or focal deficit emerges
recommendations.rationale: Absent red flags or a localizing neurological indication, advanced spinal imaging does not improve outcomes and yields incidental/degenerative findings that drive low-value downstream care; whole-spine 'screening' compounds this by imaging asymptomatic regions with no pre-test indication.
recommendations.notes: Statement is the verbatim-supported ACR/NASS principle (ACR Appropriateness Criteria: advanced spinal imaging Usually Not Appropriate absent red flags; NASS Choosing Wisely concurs). The whole-spine 'screening' order that motivated the rec (gold RC-C-02) is captured by the precondition + keywords ('whole spine' / 'whole-spine'). vv:true. Reconciliation re-seed 16-Jul-2026: re-framed statement + un-parked (was vv:false, which parked it out of the live catalog).

recommendations.statement: Don't order knee MRI as the first study for an acute knee injury; obtain weight-bearing radiographs first and reserve MRI for a suspicious exam or negative radiographs with continued suspicion of internal derangement.
recommendations.precondition: acute knee injury (within ~1-2 days) where the exam does NOT suggest significant internal derangement or fracture — no effusion/haemarthrosis, negative ligamentous and meniscal special tests (e.g., Lachman, anterior drawer negative), able to bear weight, no Ottawa Knee Rule positive findings — and radiographs have not yet been obtained. An order for knee MRI on day 1 in this low-suspicion setting is low-value.
recommendations.consider_instead: apply the Ottawa Knee Rule and obtain weight-bearing radiographs first; manage conservatively with short-interval reassessment; reserve MRI for negative radiographs with continued suspicion of occult fracture / internal derangement, or a significant effusion or positive ligament exam
recommendations.rationale: Day-1 MRI for an acute knee with a benign exam rarely changes early management, yields incidental findings, and strains access; radiographs are first-line and MRI adds value chiefly after negative radiographs or with a significant effusion / positive exam.
recommendations.notes: Anchor: ACR Appropriateness Criteria 'Acute Trauma to the Knee' (Revised 2019) — radiographs 'usually the initial imaging modality'; MRI 'Usually Appropriate' when radiographs negative but occult fracture / internal derangement suspected. Precondition carves out effusion / positive exam where a skeletally immature knee (gold case is 14F) would warrant earlier imaging. Closes gold case RC-C-04.
